reasons: orders shifting their way as high-end MLCC shortage persists
AI server demand driving sharp price gains in high-end MLCCs
mentions.text:
▶ AI server demand drives sharp price gains in high end MLCCs

- Rising demand for AI server buildouts is tightening global supply of high end MLCCs, triggering sharp price spikes in China's electronic component distribution market.

- Spot prices for some popular MLCC products have climbed 3 to 5x since the start of the year, and in Shenzhen and Shanghai there is even speculative trading in which some product prices shift on a daily basis.

- The price gains are concentrated in high capacity, high temperature products such as 22μF and 47μF. Unlike the broad based shortage of 2018, the core issue this time is an imbalance between surging AI demand and limited supply.

- Major global players such as Murata and Samsung Electro Mechanics have recently scaled back production for consumer electronics such as smartphones and PCs, shifting capacity toward high margin products for AI servers and automotive applications.

- High end MLCCs carry high technical barriers and demanding yield requirements, making it structurally difficult to add new capacity quickly. Some AI server MLCCs have risen from around 80 yuan per 1,000 units at the start of the year to more than 350 yuan.

- Original manufacturers are managing shipments more tightly than before, with orders of several million to tens of millions of units being filled at only 10 to 20% of the requested volume.

- Some overseas suppliers have revived bundling, requiring buyers of high capacity MLCCs to also purchase mid and low capacity products.

- AI servers use roughly 8 to 12x more MLCCs than standard servers. Goldman Sachs projects that MLCCs are the third largest cost item in AI servers after GPUs and memory, and that related demand will grow 4.3x from 2025 to 2030.

- That said, the price gains are concentrated in high capacity, high reliability products for AI and automotive applications rather than across the entire product range. Demand for low capacity consumer electronics MLCCs remains weak.

- Because building high end production lines takes 18 to 24 months, the shortage is likely to persist through the second half of this year and beyond 2027. China's Fenghua Advanced Technology and Chaozhou Three Circle Group could benefit as orders shift their way.
